Loden (phoropter's edge: one draft plan, served live) put a repository's one draft at draft/ on the dev server, linked from every page with rel="draft". Today the TUI reads that page as an ordinary plan. It would show the header's commit as if the draft were committed, and drop its prompts. Both are wrong in a way a person would believe. This is also this repository's first plan, and it's a draft on purpose: the TUI should be able to read the plan that describes teaching it to read drafts.

Reading only. Answering prompts is the next plan.

Decision: A draft is recognized by its header's readAt, not its URL

where internal/substrate/model.go file page

quote p.Commit = refOf(it.Get("commit"))

Because (Claude, measured): a draft's main item has entry and title like a plan, and may have no prompts, so the main item alone can't tell them apart. The profile's draft header always has readAt and the draft's sha256. On that header commit is where the anchors resolve, not what the page was generated from, so a Page keeps the two apart rather than calling both "commit". Deciding by properties, not the URL, is how the TUI already tells plans from places.

Decision: The draft opens in plan mode, labeled as a draft

where internal/tui/tui.go file page

quote s := newDocScreen(plan, ab)

Because (Claude, then Jeff): the profile says a draft's entries are "as on a plan," so one screen reads both, and the keys stay the same. Where a plan's title bar says pumice at f02528f, a draft's says draft, not committed, read at 15:39 UTC, with the anchors' commit after it. A draft has no as-built, so that half of the screen is empty. Otherwise a draft looks like a plan for now. How it should look is part of an aesthetics pass later (Jeff).

Decision: Prompts and annotations are rows after the entry they follow

where internal/substrate/model.go file page

quote d.Entries = append(d.Entries, c.entry(e, p.URL))

Because (the profile): a prompt "follows the entry (or intro) it belongs to," and so does an annotation. The microdata parser groups properties by name, so the TUI recovers which entry comes before by each item's position in the tree. A prompt row shows its kind and text, a Select's options, its fallback, and its answer when the notes have one. An annotation row shows its heading, its quote, and its comment. A row moves with j/k like an entry.

Decision: The plan list puts the draft first, when the home page links one

where internal/tui/screens.go file page

quote for i, p := range s.home.Plans {

Because (loden): every page links draft/ with rel="draft" while the draft exists, and there's at most one. A row above the plans, marked as a draft, is where a person looks first. On a built site there's no such link, so there's no row.

Decision: A key re-fetches the page

where internal/tui/tui.go file page

quote case "esc", "backspace":

Because (loden, then Jeff): the dev server re-reads the draft on every request, so refreshing is the update. The client caches pages, so r drops the cache for the current page and loads it again, keeping the cursor on the same entry when it still exists. Only r, for now (Jeff). Polling and watching the disk were the alternatives. Watching is a local fact, so it would be the TUI's to do, but the TUI can be pointed at a site it doesn't sit beside.

Decline: Answering prompts from the TUI

Because (Jeff's shelf, then Claude): writing plan.draft.notes.md is the TUI's first write, and the annotating agreement has to be restated for this repo first, along with phoropter's **If unanswered:**. That's its own plan, once phoropter's brief with the conventions arrives. This plan never writes a file.
